primary_claim: A small MLP trained to regress cubic polynomials y=x^3+ax^2+x+b develops nine SAE features in its last layer that activate on a specific linear combination t≈x+0.3a, closely resembling the substitution t=x+a/3 used in the first step of the Cardano method for solving cubic equations.

effect.metric: median best-fit linear coefficient c in t=x+ca across 9 diagonal-band SAE features (bucketed R^2 test); SAE reconstruction R^2 on held-out activations
effect.value: median c=0.3 (Cardano's a/3 is approx. 0.333); SAE reconstruction R^2=0.995 on held-out activation vectors

contradicts_or_qualifies: extends the SAE-feature interpretation and manipulation methodology used by Anthropic on LLMs (e.g. the Golden Gate Bridge feature) to a small MLP regression toy model, finding an analogous mathematically-meaningful feature
stated_future_work: train a SAE on top of the middle layers of the NN, which are often associated with more abstract thinking
study how abstractions emerge as a function of training time (epochs)
study how abstractions emerge as a function of model size/parameter count (computational boundedness)
study whether the emergence of abstractions is path-dependent
limitations_stated: feature-clamping manipulation experiments show a multiplicative/vertical-stretch effect rather than the expected horizontal-shift effect, leaving it unclear whether this confirms or refutes the Cardano-based interpretation of the diagonal-band features
the slope for the NN's diagonal-band features (median 0.3) is not exactly the Cardano method's 1/3
the NN's task (regression) is not exactly the same as Cardano's (finding roots), so the correspondence is only suggestive
a feature was identified but how it is causally used in downstream computation was not fully tested
quote: This variable is surprisingly close to the substitution $t=x+\frac{a}{3}$ operated in the first step of the Cardano method.
